name: Trade Secrets Directive
evidence_rating: thin: one descriptive litigation study; the Commission's Article 18 impact evaluation (due June 2026) was not found; no causal evidence on innovation
summary: The Trade Secrets Directive aimed to encourage innovation by giving firms the same protection for confidential know-how across the EU; the Commission cited a survey in which 40% of firms said they held back from sharing secrets. An EU-commissioned study of about 700 court cases shows litigation still varies widely between countries and rarely crosses borders. No study has measured whether the directive changed innovation, knowledge-sharing or worker mobility.

indicators.objective: The 2013 proposal (COM(2013) 813) has no financial-statement indicators; Article 18 requires an EUIPO litigation report (2021), a Commission intermediate report (2022) and an impact evaluation (2026)
Better incentives for cross-border innovation and knowledge-sharing
indicators.indicator: Willingness to share trade secrets; spending on protective measures
indicators.target_or_baseline: Baseline (2012 survey): 40% of EU firms would refrain from sharing trade secrets for fear of misuse; 35% reported higher protection spending after misappropriation
indicators.evidence: No follow-up survey or measurement found.

indicators.objective: Effective legal redress across the EU
indicators.evidence: EUIPO study of ~700 national judgments (2017-Oct 2022): litigation volumes and fora vary widely between Member States; cross-border disputes rare; most disputed secrets commercial (62%) rather than technical (33%).

indicators.objective: Innovation, employee mobility, freedom of expression
indicators.indicator: Effects on R&D, mobility and whistleblowing
indicators.evidence: No Commission impact evaluation or independent empirical study of these effects found.

literature.citation: European Commission (2013), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Directive on the protection of undisclosed know-how and business information (trade secrets), SWD(2013) 471 (executive summary SWD(2013) 472)
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Directive on the protection of undisclosed know-how and business information (trade secrets)
literature.headline: Fragmented national protection weakens incentives for cross-border innovation; 40% of firms would refrain from sharing trade secrets; misappropriation can cut turnover by up to 30%; harmonised redress expected to boost cross-border R&D cooperation
literature.summary_plain: The Commission argued that patchy national protection made firms afraid to share know-how, with 40% saying they held back, and that common rules would encourage innovation.

literature.citation: Borghi, Cogo & Khan (for EUIPO Observatory) (2023), Trade Secrets Litigation Trends in the EU, EUIPO / European Observatory on Infringements of IP Rights
literature.title: Trade Secrets Litigation Trends in the EU
literature.venue: EUIPO / European Observatory on Infringements of IP Rights
literature.method: descriptive (quantitative and qualitative analysis of ~700 national judgments, 2017-2022)
literature.headline: Litigation highly uneven across Member States; cross-border cases uncommon; disputes mostly over commercial information (62%) such as customer lists; data gaps (party identity unknown in 45% of cases)
literature.summary_plain: A study of about 700 court cases found trade-secret litigation still differs a lot between EU countries and mostly concerns commercial data such as customer lists.

literature.authors: Aplin, T., Radauer, A., Bader, M.A., Searle, N.
literature.title: The Role of EU Trade Secrets Law in the Data Economy: An Empirical Analysis
literature.venue: IIC - International Review of Intellectual Property and Competition Law
literature.method: online survey of 84 organisations (Sept 2021-Mar 2022), 51 expert interviews, 13 case studies, from a study for the European Commission
literature.outcomes: use of the Trade Secrets Directive to protect shared data; perceived gaps
literature.headline: Drawing on a survey of 84 organisations, 51 interviews and 13 case studies, the authors conclude that only very modest reform of the Trade Secrets Directive is warranted to support data sharing, favouring soft law and practical steps.
literature.summary_plain: Researchers asked companies and experts how the EU trade secrets law works when businesses share data. They found it broadly fit for purpose and recommend guidance rather than big legal changes.
literature.quality: Small convenience sample, qualitative-heavy; no outcome measurement or counterfactual
literature.citation: Aplin, T., Radauer, A., Bader, M.A., Searle, N. (2023), The Role of EU Trade Secrets Law in the Data Economy: An Empirical Analysis, IIC - International Review of Intellectual Property and Competition Law
